findings.issue: The root ErrorBoundary renders a 'Not found' page for every thrown error, so an API 500 or network failure is presented to users as a missing page and logged nowhere user-visibly.
findings.suggestion: Use isRouteErrorResponse/error.status to render 404 vs a distinct error message, and prefer per-route ErrorBoundary exports (or throw data('Not Found', { status: 404 })) as the framework docs recommend.

findings.issue: When filters shrink the result set, the displayed page is clamped to totalPages but the URL keeps the stale page=N, so the URL and rendered page disagree (and a reload honors the stale value).
findings.suggestion: Effectively replace the page param (or clamp it) in setSearchParams when the clamped page differs from the URL's.

findings.issue: spriteUrl is implemented twice (server-side in lib/pokeapi.server.ts:47 and client-side here) with the same pattern, and type.tsx:81 inlines a copy of the TypeBadge markup.
findings.suggestion: Keep one shared client-safe URL helper (the API base can be passed in) and reuse <TypeBadge> in the damage-relations list.

findings.issue: details.get(r.move)! non-null assertion spans two data structures built far apart; a future edit to either silently breaks the invariant, and the loader's pervasive any typing hides it.
findings.suggestion: Model the API responses with narrow interfaces (like the existing NamedResource) and use a safe lookup with an explicit error.

findings.issue: decodeURIComponent(params.name) re-decodes already-decoded route params and can throw a URIError on inputs like '/pokemon/%', which lands in the misleading root ErrorBoundary.
findings.suggestion: Trust params.name (or wrap the decode in try/catch and treat failure as not-found).

findings.issue: apiGet caches the in-flight promise with no timeout or AbortSignal; if the API hangs, the hung promise is cached forever and every subsequent request for that URL stalls.
findings.suggestion: Add an AbortSignal.timeout(...) to the fetch and delete the cache entry on rejection including aborts (the existing catch covers thrown errors, so this mainly needs the signal).

summary: A genuinely idiomatic, current-stable (React Router 8.5.1) framework-mode app: typed route modules, proper data()/status handling, URL-driven state, and a clean server/client data boundary. The main blemishes are a root ErrorBoundary that mislabels all errors as 'Not found', minor duplication of sprite-URL and badge helpers, and pervasive any typing in loaders. I'd merge after a small round of nits.
